images.title: Rings that show primes
images.purpose: Show how a ring around a number is cut into equal arcs, one for each prime in its factorisation, each coloured by its prime.
images.composition: Four rings in one row across the centre with the number inside each and a short factorisation under the last two, white space between.
exact_structure: Ring 1 around 2: one full teal #0072B2 ring.
Ring 2 around 3: one full amber #E69F00 ring.
Ring 3 around 6: exactly 2 equal arcs, one teal and one amber. Under it: 6 = 2 × 3.
Ring 4 around 12: exactly 3 equal arcs, two teal and one amber. Under it: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3.
Thin white gaps separate the arcs.
rejection: arcs of unequal size, or arc counts other than 1, 1, 2 and 3
the 12 ring with other than two teal arcs and one amber arc
any of the numbers 101 to 110 shown
images.takeaway: The number of arcs is the number of primes in the factorisation, and each arc wears its prime's colour.
images.description: Rings around 2 (teal), 3 (amber), 6 (teal and amber halves) and 12 (two teal thirds and one amber third).
images.context: Shown beside the puzzle text on decoding the colour scheme.
images.teaching_notes: Compare 6 and 12: one extra 2 in the factorisation adds one extra teal arc.

image_decisions.why: The puzzle is visual, so a few sample rings make the coding rule clear.
